Question: During the reading of expository texts, 4th grade elementary students present some difficulties in differentiating between the topic and the main idea. Which of the following explanations correctly establishes this difference?

Question: In the lyrical genre unit, a teacher presents to his students the following poem: In those days I was twenty years old and I was crazy. I had lost a country but had gained a dream. A wooden room, in shadows, in one of the lungs of the tropics. And sometimes I turned inside myself and visited the dream: a statue eternalized in liquid thoughts, a white worm twisting in love. An unbridled love. A dream within another dream. And the nightmare told me: you will grow up. You will leave behind the images of pain and the labyrinth and you will forget. The artillery battery allowed the soldiers to strongly resist the combat. 2. The restaurant chef decided to buy a new set of kitchenware, as the one he used was very worn out. 3. A sober show was provided by the band of musicians in their concert, demonstrating a great level in the use of the drum kit. 4. Batteries pose a real danger to children, so toys that use them must have a safety screw. The students answer that the term in sentence 4 has the same meaning as the excerpt. Question: A 5th-grade teacher whose class goal is to work with students on applying the concept of a semantic field, proposes reading the following fragment: The vegetation landscape of the Metropolitan Region is characterized by being predominantly mountainous, although in the valleys and basins the acacia steppe develops. Question: A teacher aims for his students to identify the purpose of using dialogical sequences in different narratives. To do this, he proposes reviewing different texts, including reading the following fragment: Also the poet, if he is a true poet, must perpetually repeat "I don't know". With each verse he tries to answer, but at the moment he puts the final period, doubts assail him and he begins to notice that his answer is temporary and in no way satisfactory. Then he tries again and again, so that the successive signs of his dissatisfaction with himself are held together with a huge clip by literary historians to call them "The Work." Sometimes I fantasize about improbable situations. I imagine, for example, in my audacity, that I have the opportunity to talk with Ecclesiastes, the author of a shocking lament about the vanity of all human enterprises. I would have bowed very deeply before him, as he is -at least for me- one of the most important poets. But then I would have taken him by the hand: "There is nothing new under the sun," you wrote, Ecclesiastes. Nevertheless, You yourself were born new under the sun. And the poem you created is also new under the sun, as before You nobody had written it. [...] And also I would like to ask you, Ecclesiastes, what would you like to write now, again under the sun? Something with which to complete your ideas, or maybe you're tempted to deny some of them? [...] For you will not say "I have already written everything, I have nothing to add." No poet can say this, much less one as great as You. (I don't know, Wislawa Szymborska.) Of the following questions posed by the teacher, which one enables students to recognize the purpose of the dialogical sequence in the previous fragment?
Answer A: What register of speech does the broadcaster use to address Ecclesiastes?
Answer B: What are the central themes addressed in Ecclesiastes' book according to the broadcaster?
Answer C: What is the contrast that can be drawn between literary historians and Ecclesiastes?
Answer D: What is the relationship between Ecclesiastes' reference and the idea of the transient nature of the poet's certainties?
Subdomain: Knowledge of teaching and instructional strategies

Question: A teacher is working in the Writing section with the aim of expanding the vocabulary of unfamiliar concepts. Question: Read the following situation: A teacher, whose objective of the class is to understand argumentative texts, presents the following editorial to the students: The young people rise up “Don't shoot me. I'm trying to study.” “We want a graduation, not a funeral.” Hundreds of thousands of students in the United States have risen up with slogans like this against the status quo of the arms industry that, in alliance with the individualistic and colonizing spirit that forged the country, has gained a power without too many limits. Hundreds of thousands of young people marched on Saturday on Pennsylvania Avenue in Washington between the White House and the Capitol in a “March for our Lives” supported by 800 other protests across the country. Their reading of manifestos in front of the legislators' headquarters also aimed to mark the target of their proposals: the seat of Congress. They try to focus the national political debate on gun limits several months before the elections that will renew the House of Representatives, a third of the Senate, plus the majority of state governors. Thus, the pressure grows in the streets, but it has not yet managed to make a dent in the Government. President Trump signed a budget hours before the marches that does not include special measures to curb violence. The challenge for young people is colossal, but only their persistence can make the premise that the future is in their hands a reality. (El País Newspaper). Question: Read the following situation: A teacher is working with a senior class on the following learning objective: “Recognize the phenomenon of perspectivism in contemporary literary works.” To achieve this, she presents her students with the following excerpt from the novel The Cubs by Mario Vargas Llosa: He only returned to school after the Independence Day holidays and, oddly enough, instead of having been deterred by soccer (wasn't it because of soccer, in a way, that Judas bit him?) he came back more athletic than ever. On the other hand, he started to care less about his studies. And it made sense, no fool he, he no longer needed to cram: he'd show up for exams with very low averages and the Brothers would pass him, bad exercises and excellent, poor homework and he passed. Since the accident they pampered you, we'd say, you knew nothing about fractions and, such nerve, they gave you a sixteen. Besides, they made him help in mass, Cuéllar reads the catechism, carries the year's pennant in processions, erases the blackboard, sings in the choir, hands out the notebooks, and on the first Fridays he would have breakfast even if he did not take communion. Question: A professor who is working on the characteristics of contemporary narrative wants to check the learning of narrative techniques that affect the time of the story. Question:

Question: A teacher from a 4th grade class has divided the class into groups to write a news article on different topics. What answer from the teacher could make the difference between the author and the lyrical speaker more understandable to the students, based on the previous poetic fragment?

Answer B: The author of the text differs from the lyrical speaker in that the poem constitutes a fiction whose internal mechanics do not depend on extra-literary reality, even if similarities can be found between the two planes
Answer C: Beyond the similarities that may exist between the lyrical speaker and the author's biography, the voice speaking in the poem is always a verbal construction, not a flesh-and-blood person, so author and speaker are never the same
Answer D: The lyrical speaker is not the same as the author because the reality to which the 'I' refers is a reality of discourse, which only holds value in the instance in which it is produced and does not have linguistic existence beyond the speech act that proclaims it
Subdomain: Knowledge of teaching and instructional strategies

Question: A teacher in a 7th Grade class asks the students to write a news article about the school's anniversary week. Question:
A teacher, in the unit of the lyric genre in an 8th Grade class, will conduct a summative evaluation, which contains, among other questions, the following: What is the tone of the following poem?
Despecho
Ah, I am so tired! I have laughed so much,
So much, that tears have appeared in my eyes;
So much, that this grimace that contracts my mouth
Is a strange trace of my wild laughter.
So much, that this intense pallor I have
(Like in old noble portraits)
Is due to the fatigue of the wild laughter
That slides its lethargy over my whole body.
Ah, I am so tired! Let me sleep;
For, like anguish, joy makes you sick.
What a strange occurrence to say that I am sad!
When have you seen me more joyful than now?
Lie! I have no doubts, nor jealousy,
Nor uneasiness, nor anguish, nor sorrows, nor longings,
If my eyes shine with the humidity of tears,
It is due to the effort of laughing so much...
Juana de Ibarbourou
Upon reviewing the evaluations, the teacher finds the following student's response: “The tone of the poem is joy, because the speaker says in several verses that they are laughing.”
What comment from the teacher to the student's answer could favor their identification of the tone of the evaluated poem?
Answer A: You must explain what the speaker means in the last stanza of the poem, where they establish their stance, and then identify the tone
Answer B: You managed to grasp that the poem talks about joy. However, the tone still needs to be determined. To do so, I suggest you relate the title to the content of the poem
Answer C: You identified that the emotion of the poem relates to joy, but you did not recognize the tone. You must identify the lyrical attitude and relate it to the poem's purpose
Answer D: You remained at a denotative level, failing to recognize the tone of the poem. You must underline the verses where a feeling is explicitly mentioned in the poem to determine which one prevails
Subdomain: Knowledge of teaching and instructional strategies

Question: During the narrative unit in a 6th grade class, a teacher asks the students to write a short expository text about some animal and its characteristics. Which of the following teacher's comments on the student's text would provide better formative feedback and help guide the student's learning?

Answer D: You managed to identify an animal. You should write about its characteristics: where do pandas live, what is their anatomy, what do they eat, what size are they?
Subdomain: Knowledge of assessment

Question:
For a 12th grade class, during the unit "Reality and Freedom", a teacher, in order to develop an interpretative analysis of a poetic text from a formal level, gives her students the following poem to read:
"I would be less punished if your complexion were not nardo for my sight, nardo, your skin thistle for my touch, thistle, your voice your era for my ear, your era. Your era is your voice for my ear, your era, and I burn in your voice and around you I burn, and I take time to burn what I take time to offer you my era, my voice for yours my era. Your hand is a thorn if I feel it, thorn, wave your body if I reach it, wave, close once, but a thousand not close. Heron is my sorrow, slender and sad heron, alone like a sigh and an I, alone, stubborn in her error and in her disgrace stubborn." From The Unceasing Ray, by Miguel Hernández.
Which of the following questions asked by the teacher to the students is related to an interpretative analysis from the formal level of the text?

Subdomain: Knowledge of teaching and instructional strategies

Question: In a first year high school class, a teacher proposes the following activity to students to work on vocabulary expansion: “Read the following report, which was written last year by a student after the integrated field trip activity, and replace the highlighted terms with the words noted following the text”. We did not know how to distinguish the usual song of hens and the noise they make when they are ready to brood. However, by far, the most beautiful thing we heard was the song of the swallows. Truly beautiful. Supporting words: honk – cluck – quack – gobble – chirp – cackle. To which objective related to vocabulary expansion does the previous activity correspond?

Question: A high school teacher proposes to work with the students on the identification of pronouns referring to different entities. Subdomain: Knowledge of students' understanding and development

Question:
A high school teacher works with students on reading, analyzing, and interpreting lyrical texts related to the theme of freedom. In an activity, they listen to the song “El cautivo de Til Til” and are then asked to analyze and characterize the lyrical speaker based on the following excerpt:
They say Manuel is his name
and they take him on the road to Til Til,
that the governor does not want
to see his genteel bearing along La Cañada.
They say that in war he was
the best and in the city
he dazzled like the lightning
of freedom.
(...)
They say he was like lightning
when he rode his steed
and that as the rider passed
all called him by the name Manuel.
I don’t know if I will return
to see him free and genteel,
I only know he smiled on the way
to Til Til.
El cautivo de Til Til, version by Aquelarre.
Upon reviewing the activity, the teacher comes across the following student response:
“The speaker seems to be reflecting and remembering to himself. He is somewhat sad and melancholic, but he is brave, like the lightning of freedom. This comparison made by the speaker seems very interesting to me because lightning is something that dazzles and so is freedom. He mentions the name of a place in Chile, and in general, he does not use difficult words.”
What problem does the student's response present in relation to the purpose of the activity proposed by the teacher?
Answer A: It shows a partial confusion between the subject dealt with and the voice expressed in the text
Answer B: It develops a response that strays from what was asked in the activity, as it focuses on other elements of the poem
Answer C: It focuses on personal appreciations over the content of the lyrical text to characterize the speaker
Answer D: It shows a lack of relevant references to the text in the response, as it only refers to a comparison made in it, but not with other verses
Subdomain: Knowledge of students' understanding and development

Question: A teacher of 2nd grade of secondary school tackles the writing of expository texts. Question:

Question: A teacher, who is working on argumentation with a year 3 high school class, reviews the following writing from one of her students: “Expert advisors have stated that, currently, we find ourselves with the highest gas emission index in the last three years.” Which of the following statements would constitute the most appropriate feedback to correct the agreement error presented by the term “highest” in the previous writing?

Question: A kindergarten teacher requires conducting a diagnostic assessment to explore the lexical skills of children, specifically the ability to define words and recognize which category they belong to.  What educational situation is appropriate to gather evidence regarding these skills?

Subdomain: Knowledge of assessment

Question: A fourth grade teacher is reading with his students the following excerpt from the story *The Discussion of the Hares,* by Alicia Morel:  Simon the rabbit had a ferocious appetite. Dogs or the fox that lives in the nearby forest could come," she replied, barely poking her nose out of the burrow. "What dogs or foxes! Today is truce day." "Are you sure?" Subdomain: Knowledge of teaching and instructional strategies

Question: A teacher of a 4th grade class is designing a test to assess the reading comprehension of her students through various questions related to non-literary texts. Among the selected texts, the teacher includes the following:  Bats are the only mammals equipped with wings capable of flying. One of their characteristics is that they have a very limited sense of sight, so they orient themselves and locate obstacles and food using a developed system of high-frequency ultrasounds inaudible to humans.  They are nocturnal animals that feed on insects and small animals. Like bees and other insects, bats fulfill an important function in nature: they are pollinators without which many plant species could not reproduce.  Although bats are commonly associated with being small animals, there are bats of different sizes. The smallest weighs about 1.5 grams, while the largest can weigh 1.2 kilograms and have a wingspan of 1.5 meters.  Bats are present on all continents, except Antarctica. Like mole rats, they are mammals whose body temperature depends on the environment, especially when inactive.  (Adapted from: www.nationalgeographic.com.es/animales/murcielagos).  Which of the following questions allows evaluating the extraction of implicit information from the previous text?

Answer D: Read the text: "On Sunday, the London Zoo reopened, a day after the fire that forced activities to be suspended. The London Zoo, the oldest in the world, opened its doors for the first time in 1826 and houses more than

Question: Which of the following activities specifically allows working on grammatical agreement in writing with 2nd Grade students?

Question: A teacher of middle-level children has observed that her group of boys and girls enjoys creative and exploratory experiences using their hands, and often copies letters from stories, magazines, and logos. Answer B: In small groups, ask the children to identify and repeat onomatopoeias of different animals. Then, in a new experience, have them repeat rhymes related to animals. They finish by completing simple sentences with rhymes related to animals

Finish by encouraging them to play with the puppet and create stories freely
Subdomain: Knowledge of teaching and instructional strategies

Question: A teacher in a 6th grade class is exercising reading comprehension with the students. Question: A teacher, in an 8th grade, at the end of the unit on Dramatic Genre, asks the students to create a brief text. Upon reviewing them, he finds the following creation of a student:  A house like any other. On the right, the son in the room playing on the computer, and on the left, the dad preparing tea.  DAD: Son, come have tea. This is the tenth time I've told you.  SON: I'm coming, give me a few minutes.  DAD: (Very angry) Come immediately!  SON: Yes, I'm coming, I'm just finishing a match of Free Fire.  But the dad can't take it anymore and goes angrily to talk to his son, to tell him how it's possible that he is so obsessed that he no longer spends time with his father.  SON: But dad, it’s for my future. I will be a gaming influencer! -the dad stays in the room watching his son thoughtfully-.  DAD: I just wanted to share with you the only time we can be together.  SON: Oh, I'm sorry! Just give me 5 minutes and I'll go.  And this is how another day ends in an ordinary family.  What difficulty in the process of learning to produce dramatic texts is noted in the student’s creation?
Answer A: Mixes the stage directions language with the aside
Answer B: Confuses the aside with the dialogue of the characters
Answer C: Confuses the voice of the characters with the voice of the narrator
Answer D: Does not understand the function of stage directions in a dramatic work
Subdomain: Knowledge of students' understanding and development

Question: A teacher is working on punctuation with his 7th grade students. To do this, he hands out a guide that contains the following exercise:  Read the following fragment and place the comma, when appropriate, in the underlined segment.  Sergio Gómez is a columnist, editor, Spanish teacher, and Chilean writer who owes his fame mainly to the juvenile novels he has written, particularly the series of the teenage detective Quique Hache.  The students correctly complete the activity by placing the comma in the underlined segment after the words: columnist and editor.  What prior learning do the students need to correctly apply the comma in the underlined segment?
Answer A: Recognize analogous syntactic elements
Answer B: Identify adjective subordinate clauses
Answer C: Identify the vocative within a sentence
Answer D: Distinguish conjunctive elements within a sentence
Subdomain: Knowledge of students' understanding and development

Question: During the Poetry unit in a 6th-grade class, in an evaluation context, a teacher asks the students to read the following excerpt from a poem by Nicanor Parra, so they can analyze it, identifying elements of poetic language.  Dreams  I dream of a table and a chair   I dream that I turn around in a car   I dream that I am filming a movie   I dream of a gas station   I dream that I am a luxury tourist   I dream that I am hanging from a cross   I dream that I am eating fish   I dream that I am crossing a bridge   I dream of a neon sign.    Several students comment that the poem makes no sense because it is repetitive and the lines do not connect with each other.  Considering the students' comments, what question from the teacher could guide them to make a correct interpretation of the poem?
Answer A: How does that repetition and apparent lack of meaning relate to the title of the poem?
Answer B: What rhetorical devices does the poem present that allow us to reconstruct the meaning of the lines?
Answer C: What feeling does the lyrical speaker want to express through the dreamlike images he constructs?
Answer D: What is the name of the rhetorical figure that consists of the repetition of the same phrase in several consecutive lines?
Subdomain: Knowledge of students' understanding and development

Question: A teacher, in an 8th grade class, during the unit on lyrical genre, will formatively evaluate the following objective: "Understand the formal characteristics of a poem." Which of the following activities will allow for direct evidence of achieving the proposed objective?
Answer A: Present a poem and ask students to identify the symbols of the poem and then meet in small groups to analyze them with their classmates
Answer B: Present a sonnet and a free verse poem that address the same theme and, starting from the distinction of adjectives and synonymous terms, compare the similarities and differences between both poems
Answer C: Present a poem and ask students to identify the speaker, motive, and lyrical object, to develop a written personal analysis of the text mentioning the topics present in it
Answer D: Present a poem and ask students to identify, through a guide of questions, the number of verses, stanzas, presence or absence of rhyme, meter, and characteristics of these, as well as the presence of literary figures
Subdomain: Knowledge of assessment

Question: A teacher, in a 2nd year secondary class, will conduct research with the students about the literature of the Golden Age, focusing on the characteristics and historical context of that period. After a search on the internet, the students will compile an extensive bibliography, and then select the most appropriate texts according to the purpose of the research. Which of the following activities proposed by the teacher would be the most suitable for the selection of the researched texts?

Answer B: Conduct a general reading of the texts to identify key ideas and then evaluate the relevance of the information according to the purpose of the research

Answer C: With a bone-breaker

Question: A teacher, in a 2nd year secondary class, in the unit about lyrical texts from the Golden Age, is working on the following objective: "Understand the lyrical motive in different poems." To do this, he reads together with the students the following sonnet:  Love begins with restlessness, request, fervors, and insomnia; grows with risks, lances, and claims; sustains itself with cries and pleas. Doctrinal lukewarmness and thaw, maintains being among deceitful veils, until with grievances or jealousy it extinguishes its fire with its tears. Its beginning, its middle and end is this: so why, AlciNo, do you feel the deviation of Celia, who once loved you well? What reason is there that pain costs you? For love did not deceive you, my AlciNo, but the precise term arrived.  (Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz).  Several students comment that they cannot understand the lyrical motive of the poem because they have a vocabulary that is unknown to them.  What activity should the teacher propose so that the students can understand the lyrical motive of the poem?
Answer A: Students highlight the words that hinder understanding of the poem and discuss their possible meanings with their peers
Answer B: Students assign possible meanings to the difficult words and verify them with the help of the teacher
Answer C: Students reflect on the meanings they assign to the difficult words and write sentences with them
Answer D: Students select the words that are difficult to understand and replace them with others that, according to their prior knowledge, have similar meanings
Subdomain: Knowledge of students' understanding and development

Question: A teacher, in a 1st grade secondary class, conducts a group oral reading of the story El padre, by Olegario Lazo, with the aim of verifying, during the reading, whether the students understand what they are reading.  What reading comprehension strategy would be suitable to address the proposed learning objective?
Answer A: Students summarize what they are reading
Answer B: Students identify the most important ideas of the story
Answer C: Students formulate questions about what they read and answer them
Answer D: Students relate the information from the story to their experiences
Subdomain: Knowledge of teaching and instructional strategies

Question: In a 3rd Year secondary class, a teacher is reinforcing the interpretive level of reading comprehension. To do this, she presents the following excerpt for analysis:  Self-Portrait   I have spent three years and three months abroad. I prefer to look to the left. A friend of mine enjoys betrayal. The end of a trip left me with the same sad aftertaste as the end of a novel. He forgot what I disliked. It is possible that I have unknowingly spoken to someone who has killed someone. I will look in the dead ends. What lies at the end of life does not scare me. In reality, I do not listen to what I am told. I am surprised that I am given a nickname without barely knowing me. It takes me time to realize that someone is behaving badly towards me; it seems so surprising that something like this could happen to me: evil is, in a way, immoral. Archive. At two years old, I spoke with Salvador Dalí. Competition does not motivate me. Describing my life accurately would take me more time than living it.  After the reading, some students mention that they do not understand how the different sentences are connected in the text.   What question from the teacher could guide the students in analyzing the previous excerpt?
Answer A: How does the enumeration of incoherent facts relate to the title of the text?
Answer B: What association can be established between the painter Salvador Dalí and the actions described?
Answer C: What narrative device characteristic of contemporary literature is used in the text?
Answer D: How does the narrator's mood relate to the facts they enumerate?
Subdomain: Knowledge of teaching and instructional strategies

Question: A secondary teacher, in the 4th grade, in the unit of Contemporary Narrative, is reviewing narrative procedures specific to contemporary literature. After explaining the concept of polyphony in literature and giving some examples, she checks that some students still do not fully understand what it consists of. To facilitate comprehension, she decides to explain this concept through an analogy.  What analogy could the teacher present to facilitate the understanding of polyphony in literature?
Answer A: The choir of a school sings the institution's hymn for a civic act
Answer B: A group of friends meets after vacation to share their photos and experiences
Answer C: A person is in a square and comments on the behavior of the children playing there
Answer D: When a flowerpot falls from a balcony onto a parked car, witnesses recount what they saw
Subdomain: Knowledge of teaching and instructional strategies

Question: A secondary teacher, in 1st grade, is working on the following objective: "Determine the truthfulness and consistency of information from various sources." In this regard, she proposes that the students review information about vaccines.  What activity would be appropriate to suggest to the students to meet the stated learning objective?
Answer A: Choose ten different sources that address the same topic, then compare them and identify what similar information appears in the greatest number of chosen media
Answer B: Investigate various specialized sources on the topic, then look for what information they present about it and what organization supports it
Answer C: Arrange an interview with a specialist they know who is knowledgeable on the topic to ask them the questions that arose during the research, and then draw conclusions
Answer D: Create and conduct a survey of people who are for and against vaccines, and then draw conclusions based on the results
Subdomain: Knowledge of teaching and instructional strategies

Question: In the 1st Year, a secondary teacher is working on grammatical correction in written production in formal contexts, considering, among other aspects, the appropriate agreement of verbs. In this instance, a student asks why the singular use of the verb 'haber' is recommended in sentences like 'There were many difficulties during the educational process', and not 'There were many difficulties during the educational process', if what follows is in plural: 'many difficulties'.  What explanation from the teacher would allow for a conceptually precise and comprehensible response to the student's doubt?
Answer A: The verb 'There was' denotes the presence of subjects or situations, and in this case, it is used within a periphrastic passive sentence in which the subject, 'the educational process', functions as an agent complement that usually appears postponed at the end of the sentence
Answer B: The verb 'There was' does not establish its agreement in number with the part of the sentence 'many difficulties', but with 'the educational process', which functions as the subject of this sentence, therefore the grammatical rule of agreement between subject and verb is fulfilled
Answer C: The verb 'There was' connects with the noun phrase 'many difficulties', because this is part of its predicate. Therefore, the fact that this element is plural does not affect the verb, since in this case, the conjugated form of 'to have' functions as an auxiliary verb of another one that has been omitted
Answer D: The verb 'There was' expresses the existence of what is referred to after 'many difficulties', which functions as a direct complement in this sentence that lacks a subject. The fact that it appears in plural does not imply that the verb must be, since it must agree with the subject, not with the direct complement
Subdomain: Knowledge of students' understanding and development

Question: A secondary teacher, in a 4th year class, is working with his students on intertextuality, through the reading of the following micro-story:  Sleeping Beauty closes her eyes but does not sleep. She is waiting for the prince. And when she hears him approaching, she simulates an even deeper sleep. Nobody has told her, but she knows. She knows that no prince passes by a woman who has her eyes wide open.  After the reading, a student makes the following comment: "In this micro-story, just like in the classic tale, Sleeping Beauty is still waiting for the prince. In other words, the hero of the story is the prince."  In response to this comment, what question from the teacher could guide the student to make a correct interpretation of the intertextual relationship present in the previous micro-story?
Answer A: What structural elements does the micro-story present in relation to the classic tale?
Answer B: Do you think the characters of the micro-story are relevant today?
Answer C: What are the main characteristics of the characters in both stories?
Answer D: Why does the Sleeping Beauty of the micro-story pretend to sleep, unlike the original version?
Subdomain: Knowledge of students' understanding and development

Question: A teacher, in a 2nd year Middle School class, is working with her students on the following objective: "Recognize the effects that literary figures produce in poems." To address this, the teacher asks them to read different poems and requests them to recognize the literary figures present in them, so that they can later analyze what effect the use of these figures has on the overall meaning of the poem. One of the poems she presents is the following:    FELINE    Time feels like it is sliding over the skin   as if it were a cat's tongue   sinuous, humid, slightly rough    You can feel its claws:   and all that remains of us   are the remnants of a silent feast    Time jumps and digs through the trash   and only finds thorns    (Óscar Hahn).    The teacher, upon reviewing the students' answers, finds that several of them point out that the comparison is the predominant figure in the poem because the feline is compared to the passage of time.    What question from the teacher would help the students recognize the metaphor as the figure that predominates in the poem?
Answer A: What rhetorical device gives meaning to the poem?
Answer B: What characteristics does the lyrical object of the poem possess?
Answer C: What relationship is established between the characteristics of the feline and the passage of time?
Answer D: What feelings does the lyrical speaker express through the image of the feline?
Subdomain: Knowledge of students' understanding and development

Question: A 2nd year secondary teacher, after conducting a written production in which students had to comment on a novel, reviews the following text from one of them:  The novel presents a very complex argument related to the lack of trust between the characters. The novel is structured in three parts, thus the novel is complex to understand. Finally, the novel made me reflect on the lack of empathy in the world we live in, such as within the novel, the character Pedro, who does not help his mother when she needed him.  Which of the following observations, made by the teacher, provides feedback to the student to improve the cohesion of the text?
Answer A: It is necessary that you use coreference to improve your text
Answer B: To avoid repetition, use equivalent words for: the novel
Answer C: Avoid lexical repetition: the novel is repeated several times in the paragraph
Answer D: The text fails in its explicit relationships by incurring in lexical repetition
Subdomain: Knowledge of students' understanding and development

Question: A 3rd year teacher, during the Oral Argumentation unit, develops a discussion activity about energy efficiency. In this instance, one student defends the idea that a call should be made to not "waste" energy. Another student questions this stance, as they consider that it would be very subjective to classify the uses simply as wasting or not wasting. The teacher asks the first student to reformulate their idea.  What strategy would allow the student to reformulate their ideas more precisely within the presented discussion?
Answer A: Use of consecutive sequences to specify the effects of wasting energy
Answer B: Use of additive sequences to add ideas related to other inefficient ways of using energy
Answer C: Use of explanatory sequences to determine the concrete meaning of what would constitute energy waste
Answer D: Use of adversative sequences to establish partial contrasts between different wasteful uses of energy
Subdomain: Knowledge of teaching and instructional strategies

Question: In a 6th-grade class, a teacher is working with the students on understanding the moods conveyed by poems. To do this, together with the class, she performs the following reading:  Can we sit in the shade   and contemplate the garden?   Sad herbs are growing.   The trees enclose us   and in their long throats   the silence cries.    (Our blood   also cries,   dark river   that begins   and ends   in us).    Beyond us, heavy mountains   halt us   and the moon rises   as an eye.   ( The Water Cycle, Alicia Montal).  What strategy can the teacher propose to the students to enhance the understanding of the mood conveyed in the poem read?
Answer A: Identify the rhetorical figures present in the poem
Answer B: Answer the question: what other title would you give to the poem?
Answer C: Relate the characteristics of the garden to what the speaker expresses
Answer D: Name characteristics of gardens known to the students and the feelings they generate
Subdomain: Knowledge of teaching and instructional strategies

Question: A teacher in a 5th grade works on highlighting as a tool to help students identify the main ideas in non-literary texts. During the activities, the teacher notices that the students highlight a large part of the text to work on, without distinguishing between central and accessory content. Which of the following activities enables students to distinguish the main ideas of a text?
Answer A: List ideas using this question: what ideas are mentioned in each paragraph?
Answer B: Write down, in front of each paragraph of the text, the answer to this question: what is the paragraph about?
Answer C: Write sentences present in the text, based on this question: what is interesting in each paragraph?
Answer D: Color secondary ideas of each paragraph differently after answering this question: why do such ideas contribute to the paragraph?
Subdomain: Knowledge of teaching and instructional strategies

Question: In an 8th grade class, a teacher asks the students to read the following microstory 'Parable' by Wislawa Szymborska and then to formulate questions that guide the interpretation of the text.  Certain fishermen pulled a bottle from the bottom.   Inside the bottle was a piece of paper, and on the paper these words: "Help!, I'm here. The ocean threw me onto a deserted island. I am on the shore and waiting for help. Hurry up! I'm here!"   –It has no date. It is surely too late. The bottle might have floated for a long time – said the first fisherman.   –And the place is not indicated. It's not even known which ocean – said the second fisherman.   –Neither too late nor too far. The island 'Here' is everywhere – said the third fisherman.   The atmosphere became uncomfortable, silence fell. General truths have that problem.  Which of the following questions formulated by the students leads to an interpretation of the read story?
Answer A: What is the meaning of the phrase 'The island "Here" is everywhere'?
Answer B: What would the ending of the story have been if the message had been more precise?
Answer C: Why do the fishermen feel uncomfortable with the answer of the third man?
Answer D: If you had found a bottle with that message, what would you have done and why?
Subdomain: Knowledge of teaching and instructional strategies

Question: A teacher is working on the production of informational articles with the 5th-grade students, following a writing plan.  What activity is suitable for the students to review the overall coherence of their texts?
Answer A: Read the draft and create a concept map. Then, review the resulting thematic hierarchy and, if necessary, reorganize the information in the draft
Answer B: Read the draft and make a list of the ideas present in the text. Then, check if any information needs to be elaborated further to provide greater foundation to the text
Answer C: Read the draft to a classmate and ask them to review the text, pointing out any issues with fluency or repetitions. Then, correct the draft based on the suggestions made by the classmate
Answer D: Read the draft and highlight it
Subdomain: Knowledge of teaching and instructional strategies

Question: A teacher will be working with sixth-grade students on argumentative texts. To exemplify their characteristics, she shows the following advertisement:  LET'S TAKE CARE OF WATER!  LET'S BE RESPONSIBLE IN TIMES OF SCARCITY.  www.inae.gob.h  A student raises their hand and asks why the above advertisement is classified as an argumentative text and not as an informative text, since it provides objective information about the amount of water that is wasted by opening a faucet for 1 minute.  Which of the following interventions by the teacher is a response to the student's inquiry?
Answer A: Because providing information in an advertisement is key for the consumer to know the characteristics of the product being offered to them
Answer B: Because advertising, like publicity, has the function of convincing, with the intention that the receiver adheres to an idea or consumes a product
Answer C: Because advertising can provide information as a means of persuasion, that is, as a way of convincing people to adhere to the point of view it presents
Answer D: Because textual classifications do not always reflect the linguistic complexity of texts, as in this advertisement that serves both to inform and to convince
Subdomain: Knowledge of students' understanding and development

Question: In a 5th grade classroom, a teacher will evaluate how much her students have learned about the structure of dramatic works. To do this, she is drafting different indicators that guide the search for evidence of the learnings obtained.  Which of the following evaluation indicators accounts for the understanding of conflict in the dramatic genre?
Answer A: Distinguish the actions performed by the characters in a dramatic work
Answer B: Recognize the stereotypes represented by the characters in a dramatic work
Answer C: Identify the motivations of the protagonist and antagonist in a dramatic work
Answer D: Relate the actions of the protagonist and antagonist in a dramatic work to their own experiences
Subdomain: Knowledge of assessment

Question: A fifth-grade teacher is evaluating, through various tasks that include open questions, the following objective: "To critically evaluate the information present in non-literary texts, according to their purposes and characteristics." To do so, she presents her students with the following evaluation task:  Read the following text and then answer the questions.  Cigarettes in the Sand  Mr. Director:  I am 12 years old and, like every summer, I went to the beach with my family. While playing in the sand, I found many cigarettes thrown on the ground. Since I was a child, it has bothered me a lot that the bucket has more cigarettes than sand. So, I thought about writing to the newspapers to ask all the readers who smoke to please try not to smoke at the beach. And if they do, to please not throw the butts in the sand. That way, we kids can play in the sand with sand, and not with cigarettes.  Ignacia Tokman Herrera   www.biohechil.cl    What is the communicative purpose of the letter written by Ignacia Tokman? Why?  One of the students responds as follows: "The purpose of Ignacia is to be able to play with sand when she goes to the beach, because that is what she wants to do according to what she writes in the letter." The teacher tells him: "Yes!, you are right, according to what she writes, Ignacia wishes to be able to play at the beach with sand that does not have butts."  Which of the following questions complements the teacher's comment so that the student can better handle the evaluation objective?
Answer A: But who does she really direct her letter to?
Answer B: But what change does she want to generate with her letter?
Answer C: But what does her annoyance explained in the letter consist of?
Answer D: But why is the issue raised in her letter important for everyone?
Subdomain: Knowledge of assessment

Question: A teacher is working with 7th grade students on writing a text with an argumentative purpose about globalization. In the draft review stage, the teacher aims to verify if the students have been able to adapt their writings to the purposes of the argumentative text regarding the clear presentation of their viewpoints. One of the students submits the following draft:  The benefits of globalization  Currently, thanks to globalization, we can travel all over the world and communicate with people regardless of where they are. Moreover, Chile exports fruits or other products, and the electronic devices that arrive from abroad are produced in places like Europe, the United States, or China. This way, we can share among all people the different things that our countries produce.  Which of the following comments from the teacher encourages the student to improve her performance concerning the proposed objective for the text revision stage?
Answer A: Very well presented the positive aspects of globalization. But how could you convince your readers that globalization is beneficial?
Answer B: You have synthesized some positive aspects of globalization very well. But how could you communicate the different consequences of globalization to your readers?
Answer C: You have synthesized some positive aspects of globalization very well. But how could you express in one sentence or concept what you think about globalization?
Answer D: Very well presented the positive aspects of globalization. But how could you nuance the different challenges that globalization poses to people?
Subdomain: Knowledge of students' understanding and development

Question: A teacher, in a 2nd year Middle School class, is working on the following objective: "Consistently use literary styles." After presenting examples of the different styles and answering the students' questions, he asks them to write a brief text in indirect narrative style, based on the following vignette:  In response to this activity, a student tells the teacher: "I still don't understand how to do an indirect style. Can you explain how to do it to me?". Which of the following instructions from the teacher guides the student in creating a text in indirect style?
Answer A: Imagine a dialogue with each character from the vignette, allowing them to speak for themselves. Once you have the dialogue clear, write it down
Answer B: Observe each character from the vignette and imagine a story around them. Then, write the thoughts of the characters in that story
Answer C: Give each character from the vignette a name and write a short story that contains introductory verbs, the use of colons, and a different perspective for each character
Answer D: Write a dialogue expressing verbatim what the characters of the vignette say. Then, write that same dialogue as if you were explaining what they say
Subdomain: Knowledge of teaching and instructional strategies

Question: A teacher in the 2nd year of high school is working with his students on the interpretation of figurative language. To approach this learning, he is reading the following poem with his students:  TO WRITE  like a castaway like an exile like a nomad like a stateless person Keeping a distance from the power of money from vanity from cowardice Prefer the open air to enclosed spaces risk to security movement to safety Poetry is not a fixed place Poetry is a path A footprint in the dunes whose trace is followed knowing that it leads nowhere. (Jaime Pinos).  Which of the following instructions from the teacher guides the students in the interpretative reading task they should perform?
Answer A: I recommend that they investigate the production context of the poem and what themes characterize the poet, and then the relationship with the presented poem
Answer B: I advise them to first underline all the literary figures present in the text and then determine to which figures they correspond and, therefore, what is the correct way to read them
Answer C: I suggest they look for all the words they do not understand from the poem, such as nomad, castaway, and stateless, and determine how they relate to one another
Answer D: I suggest they look at the title first to determine what it is about and then start making associations between the key words that describe the subject, what those words literally mean, and the sensations they provoke
Subdomain: Knowledge of teaching and instructional strategies

Question: A teacher, in 1st Year, is working with her students on the inferential level of reading. To do this, she applies the strategy of interrogating the following Micro-story, formulating questions that address the inferential level:  We loved to play in the dirt yard. We chased the hens. The Laucha would "hypnotize" them. He would circle them and place them on the ground. With a little wooden stick, he drew their cage. Everything was magic. The mountain in the distance. The sound of the wind. And my mom from the window watched us grow. One Sunday, an unruly dog took my dad away from us. My mom died in life. "She has gone, my daughter," said the little girl, "take care of your mom." I grew up suddenly at twelve years old. Until I arrived in Santiago, I had no idea we were poor.  (Childhood, Pablo Ortiz Tirado. Santiago in A Hundred Words).  Which of the following questions addresses the inferential level of the narrative?
Answer A: Why does the protagonist claim to have grown up suddenly?
Answer B: What elements of the story connect the protagonist with her childhood?
Answer C: Would you have felt poor, like the protagonist, when moving from the countryside to the city? Why?
Answer D: In what way did the Laucha hypnotize the hens?
Subdomain: Knowledge of teaching and instructional strategies

Question: A teacher, in a 3rd year of high school, is working with her students on the following objective: "Recognize narrative styles". To do this, she explains the characteristics of each style, then presents some examples and provides a guide for students to identify the styles in various excerpts.  One of the excerpts in free indirect style is as follows:  "Charles was surprised by the whiteness of his nails. They were bright, sharp at the tips, more polished than the ivories of Dieppe, and almond-shaped. But the hand was not pretty, perhaps not pale enough, and somewhat horse-like in the phalanges; it was also too long and lacked the soft influences of the lines on the contours. What was beautiful were the eyes; although they were brown, they looked black because of the eyelashes, and his gaze came with frankness and warm boldness."  (Madame Bovary, Gustave Flaubert).  One of the students responds that the excerpt has an indirect style because there is a third-person narrator.  Considering this response, what content related to narrative styles is necessary for the teacher to refer to so that the student understands the free indirect style?
Answer A: Identification of narrative focalizations in a story
Answer B: Recognition of the types of narrators in a story
Answer C: Distinction between the narrator's voice and that of the characters in a story
Answer D: Knowledge of where the narrator stands in relation to the story
Subdomain: Knowledge of students' understanding and development

Question: A teacher, in a 4th Year secondary class, will evaluate the following objective: "Understand the characteristics of an epigram, in the context of interpreting lyrical works of the 20th century". Which of the following indicators accounts for the evaluated objective?

Subdomain: Knowledge of assessment

Question: A teacher, in a 3rd Year Middle School class, will evaluate, through a written test, the following objective: "Understand the role that various characters play in the conflict of the story, based on the reading of a tale." Which of the following indicators accounts for the achievement of the evaluated learning?
Answer A: They identify the types of relationships between the characters and their impact on the story

Answer D: They classify each character according to their degree of importance in the story, indicating how they determine the development of events
Subdomain: Knowledge of assessment

Question: A teacher in the 1st year of secondary school asks his students to create a written production on a topic of their choice. In the review stage, the teacher corrects the following text from one of the students:  It is important to take care of nature, especially now that we are at a critical moment in which the most serious fact, according to scientists, is that we are living at a point of no return, where the planet does not have enough time to regenerate the resources that have been exhausted by us.
